transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Hello Mr. Mbeki, thank you for coming back in to see me.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I really can't stay long. I have to get back to the shop, I'm already behind on the inventory.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand. I wanted to talk to you about your wife's delivery and some information that didn't get communicated correctly.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: What do you mean? The other doctor told me everything was fine.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: There was a mistake. Your wife tested positive for Group B strep during her pregnancy. That's a common bacteria, and the standard is to give antibiotics during labor to prevent the baby from getting an infection. However, that positive result was in the record but the labor team didn't see it, so she didn't get the medication.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Wait, she didn't get the medicine? Why are you telling me this now?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'm sorry for any confusion here. We were just incredibly busy on the floor that night.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Busy is not an excuse. My daughter is in the NICU. Is that why she's in there?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It's a possible contributing factor. Does that make sense so far?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't care if it makes sense. I care if my child is sick because you people forgot a piece of paper.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand that's frustrating. But we are monitoring the baby's white blood cell count right now.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Frustrating? My business is losing money every hour I sit in this waiting room and my kid is in an incubator.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I have to go check on another patient in a few minutes, so let's wrap this up. I just want you to know we're doing our best.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You're rushing me now? After you tell me you messed up?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'm just trying to be efficient with the time.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I want to know exactly what happens next. Who is responsible for this?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The system for flagging these results failed us. We'll probably look into the charts and see how to fix it for the future.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: That doesn't tell me when I can take my daughter home.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We will keep an eye on her. Just stay tuned for an update from the nursing staff.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: That's not a plan. Is she going to be okay or not?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'm sure it will be fine. We'll just see how the next few labs look.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I can't keep coming back here every day. I have a business to run.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I hear you. I really do.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You don't hear me. You're barely looking at me.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'm just trying to get through the facts. The baby is stable, though we have to be cautious.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: If she's stable, why is she still in the NICU?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Because of the risk of sepsis from the strep. We are giving her antibiotics now.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Why wasn't this explained to me yesterday?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We were still gathering the timeline of events.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: This is unbelievable.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Look, I really do need to get to my other patient.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: And my daughter is still in a plastic box.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We'll keep her monitored. I'll let the nurse know you're concerned.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I'm not concerned. I'm angry.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You keep saying that. You aren't saying anything.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I've explained the error. The antibiotics were missed.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: And now?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We'll just see how the next few hours go.

H.justification: Resident uses rushing language repeatedly ('let's wrap this up', 'trying to be efficient', 'need to get to my other patient').

E.justification: The error (missed GBS antibiotics) was named explicitly in the second turn using lay language and comprehension was checked once ('Does that make sense so far?'), but false reassurance was given ('I'm sure it will be fine').

A.justification: The apology ('I'm sorry for any confusion') is diluted by an immediate excuse ('We were just incredibly busy') and responsibility is later deflected to 'the system'.

R.justification: Resident relies on generic validation ('I understand', 'I hear you') and frequently meets emotional bids with factual redirection.

T.justification: No concrete plan or timeline provided; resident uses placeholders like 'stay tuned', 'we'll keep an eye on her', and 'see how the next few hours go'.
